name: Horn of Gondor
oracle_text:
When Horn of Gondor enters, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.
{3}, {T}: Create X 1/1 white Human Soldier creature tokens, where X is the number of Humans you control.
blocked_sentences: When Horn of Gondor enters, create a 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token.
{3}, {T}: Create X 1/1 white Human Soldier creature tokens, where X is the number of Humans you control.

needs.what: A 1/1 white Human Soldier creature token registered in the token pool -- suggested id `human_soldier_1_1_w`, following the existing multi-subtype naming convention (`vampire_rogue_1_1_b_lifelink`, `frog_lizard_3_3_g`): types ["Creature"], subtypes ["Human", "Soldier"], power 1, toughness 1, colors ["W"], color_identity ["W"], is_token true. Both of this card's abilities create it, so one token definition unblocks the whole card. More generally, either the token pool grows ahead of the cards that reference it, or `create_token` learns an inline token definition so a card can print the token it makes.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `create_token` names a token by card id and nothing else: `loader.py:1794` rejects the op without a `token` key, and `validate_token_references` at `loader.py:2161-2169` raises `create_token references unknown card` for any id that is not already a loaded token card -- there is no inline `power`/`toughness`/`colors`/`subtypes` form. The 30 tokens currently defined (24 in `data/cards/tokens.cards.json`, 4 in `zurgo.cards.json`, 2 in `isperia.cards.json`) contain the two halves of this token separately and never together: `human_1_1_w` (`data/cards/zurgo.cards.json:147`) is a 1/1 white Human with no Soldier subtype, and `soldier_1_1_w` (`data/cards/isperia.cards.json:1361`) is a 1/1 white Soldier with no Human subtype. Substituting either is not a cosmetic loss on *this* card, because the tokens feed the count that makes more of them: with `soldier_1_1_w` the tokens are not Humans, so X ("the number of Humans you control") never grows and the Horn's own output stops counting itself -- silently converting an engine into a flat one-shot; with `human_1_1_w` the tokens are not Soldiers, which is the half a Soldier lord or a Soldier-typed cost reads. Building the token at resolution out of the pieces does not work either: the `add_subtype` op writes `added_subtypes` onto an object chosen by a selector (`primitives.py:408-429`), and `create_token` returns no binding for the tokens it just made, so there is nothing to point that op at -- and even if there were, the resulting permanent's *printed* type line would still be wrong, which is what a static filter reading printed characteristics would see. The `tokens` expectation key also asserts a token id, so any substitute would have the verification assert a token this card does not print.

rest_is_expressible: Everything except the token id already loads. Sentence 1 is a `self_enters` trigger (in `trigger_events`) whose effect is `{"op": "create_token", "token": "human_soldier_1_1_w"}`. Sentence 2 is an activated ability with `cost` `{"mana": "{3}", "tap": true}` (both in `cost_keys`) and effect `{"op": "create_token", "token": "human_soldier_1_1_w", "amount": {"count": {"zone": "battlefield", "controller": "you", "subtypes": ["Human"], "count": "all"}}}` -- `count` is in `value_keys` and the `create_token` + `amount` shape is exactly what `data/cards/zurgo.cards.json:275-291` (Secure the Wastes) uses. The moment `human_soldier_1_1_w` exists this card can be authored with no other engine work, and its expectation would read `tokens` = 1 (the enters trigger; the activated ability is never activated in the sandbox) with `battlefield_count` 34.
